evidence.quote: Men were excluded from the analyses if they did not complete the dietary questionnaire or if the dietary information was incomplete (n=2022), leaving a total of 27 111 men for analyses.
Over a median follow-up of 11 years, 344 men were diagnosed with bladder cancer among those who were eligible for the analyses in this study.
Dietary intakes of alpha-carotene, beta-carotene, lycopene, lutein/zeaxanthin, beta-cryptoxanthin, vitamins A, E, and C, and folate were not related to the risk of bladder cancer.
Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the relative risks and 95% confidence intervals and to simultaneously adjust for age, smoking history, energy intake and intervention group.

cases.excerpt: To examine the relation of the total intake of fluids and the types of beverages to the risk of bladder cancer, we conducted a hospital based case-control study with 130 newly diagnosed bladder cancer patients and the same number of matched controls.

comparison.excerpt: Information of total fluid intake was derived from the reported frequency of consumption of the different types of beverages on the food frequency questionnaire.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Multivariate logistic regression model showed consumption of: soda (OR=8.32; 95%CI=3.18-21.76), coffee (OR=1.46; 95%CI=1.05-2.01) and spirits (OR=1.15; 95%CI=1.04-1.28) as statistically significant risk factors, while mineral water (OR=0.52; 95%CI=0.34-0.79), skim milk (OR=0.38; 95%CI=0.16-0.91), yogurt (OR=0.34; 95%CI=0.12-0.97) and frequency of daily urination (OR=0.27; 95%CI=0.18-0.41) were statistically significant protective variables.

rationale.q1: Exposure groups drawn from the same prospective MCCS cohort recruited in 1990–1994; common eligibility rules.
rationale.q10: Censoring is described; no explicit assessment or weighting for differential incomplete follow-up reported.
rationale.q11: Cox models use age as time scale; Schoenfeld residual checks and sex stratification address proportional hazards; site-specific category contrasts and CIs reported.
rationale.q2: All participants completed the same baseline 121-item FFQ, with separate regular and diet soft drink questions.
rationale.q3: Discussion explicitly states soft drink measures were self-reported and were not specifically validated.
rationale.q4: Potential confounders identified using a directed acyclic graph; socioeconomic status, alcohol, country of birth, diet, activity, sex and smoking stated.
rationale.q5: Multivariable Cox models adjust specified confounders; ASB additionally adjusts SSB and waist circumference; sensitivity analyses evaluate alternatives.
rationale.q6: Baseline cancer history excluded before follow-up.
rationale.q7: Incident invasive/metastatic primary cancers identified through Victorian Cancer Registry or Australian Cancer Database.
rationale.q8: Baseline 1990–1994 through 30 June 2013 is sufficient duration; end of follow-up explicitly stated.
rationale.q9: Death and last known presence in Australia are censoring events; proportion lost to cancer follow-up and reasons are not enumerated.

results.poolability_reason: Direct primary contrast; criterion-level Moderate JBI cohort assessment.
